uncertain_sources: Several ASR lines around 00:27 are corrupt; the proper-distance derivative and metric transformation are reconstructed from the surrounding derivation and verified blackboard equations.
The lecture uses curvature as a tidal scale. The chapter specifies orthonormal Riemann components so the dimensional estimate is not confused with the Schwarzschild Ricci scalar, which vanishes.
The lecture calls the regular drawing Kruskal coordinates. The chapter distinguishes the exact global Kruskal coordinates from their local near-horizon Rindler form.
The Wheeler interlude includes a lengthy personal anecdote. Its biographical point and the political contrast are retained without reproducing incidental private detail as technical content.
The classroom extrapolation from Alice and Charlie to many widely separated infallers is qualified: each claimed observation must be checked by an actual null ray.
The horizon-growth problem posed after 01:33 is explicitly deferred in the lecture and remains deferred rather than receiving a fabricated static-diagram answer.
The light-crossing times, cosmic black-hole count, and mountain-mass evaporation comparison are preserved as rough lecture-era estimates rather than current measured values.
The evaporating endpoint and micro-black-hole discussion are marked as semiclassical or speculative where the classical Schwarzschild diagram is insufficient.
